app.name: Bugaboo
error.auth.wrong-credentials: The e-mail address or the password is not right.
error.auth.wrong-second-step-code: That code is not right. Check the code in your app, or use one of your backup codes.
error.auth.wrong-setup-code: That setup code is not right. Copy it again from the window where Bugaboo is running.
error.auth.password-too-short: Choose a password with at least 12 characters. Length matters more than special characters.
error.auth.password-breached: That password is on lists of passwords that are tried first. Please choose another one.
error.auth.invitation-invalid: This invitation does not work. It may have run out or been used already. Ask for a new one.
error.auth.sign-up-refused: You cannot sign up here. Ask an administrator to invite you.
error.auth.passkey-rejected: The passkey could not be checked. Please try again.
error.request.wrong-token: Your sign-in does not fit this page any more. Sign in again and then try again.
error.auth.second-step-required: Before you go on, set up your second step. Your administrator asks for it, and it keeps your account safe even if your password leaks.
error.auth.access-key-not-allowed: An access key cannot do that. Sign in with your password to change your own sign-in details.
error.access.forbidden: You are not allowed to do that.
error.request.invalid: Something in your request is not valid. Check what you typed and try again.
error.request.unknown-field: We could not find one of the fields you asked for. Check the field names and try again.
error.request.bad-cursor: This list changed. Start again from the top.
error.request.wrong-origin: That did not come from a Bugaboo page. Reload the page and try again.
error.request.method-not-allowed: Bugaboo does not do that here.
error.request.timed-out: Your request took too long to arrive. Please try again.
error.request.too-large: That is too big to send.
error.edit.version-changed: Someone changed this while you were working. Use Compare and save to keep your changes.
error.edit.lock-lost: Your editing time ran out. Your text is kept as a draft. Use Compare and save to keep your changes.
error.edit.taken-over: Someone took over the editing. Your text is kept as a draft. Use Compare and save to keep your changes.
error.rate-limit.exceeded: Too many tries. Please wait a little and try again.
error.server.unavailable: Bugaboo is not available right now. Please try again in a moment.
error.server.internal: Something went wrong on our side. Nothing you did caused this.
setting.security.session-idle-minutes.he: How many minutes without activity pass before people are signed out automatically. Between 5 minutes and 24 hours.
setting.security.two-step-required.help: Ask everyone to use two-step sign-in. People who have not set it up are asked to do so the next time they sign in.
How many hours a sign-in can last at most, even when somebody keeps working. After that, people sign in again. Between 1 hour and 30 days (720 hours).
setting.auth.access-key-default-days.hel: How many days a new access key lives when the person picks no other date. Between 1 and 365 days.
setting.auth.access-key-longest-days.hel: The most days an access key can live, whatever date the person picks. Between 1 and 365 days.
setting.auth.sign-up-enabled.help: Let people make an account on their own, without an invitation. Bugaboo cannot check that an address belongs to the person until e-mail is available, so use this only on a network you trust.
setting.content.image-hosts.name: Hosts that images may come from
setting.content.image-hosts.help: The hosts that may show images in descriptions and comments, as a list separated by commas, like images.example.com. Write only the host name, without https:// and without a path. Leave the list empty to show no image from other hosts.
setting.auth.sign-up-domains.help: The e-mail domains that may sign up on their own, as a list separated by commas, like example.com. Leave the list empty to let every address sign up while signing up is on, so write your domains in first.
setting.ui.locked-why: An administrator chose this for everyone, so you can't change it here.
setting.ui.lock-help: While this is locked, nobody can choose their own value.
setting.ui.source-hidden-project: From a project you can't see
setting.ui.example-moment: Right now, a time looks like this: {moment}
setting.page.region-intro: These choices are kept with you, so they follow you to every browser you sign in from.
setting.page.start-page-intro: Choose the page Bugaboo opens after you sign in.
setting.page.sign-in-rules-intro: How long people stay signed in, and the rules for signing in. They apply to everybody.
setting.page.security-intro: What the text that people write may show.
setting.page.themes-intro: The organization's choice of look. People can choose their own, unless you lock a setting.
setting.appearance.mode.help: The colors Bugaboo uses on your screen. Match my device follows the light or dark setting of your device.
setting.appearance.light-theme.help: The theme Bugaboo shows when your device is light. It counts when you choose Match my device.
setting.appearance.dark-theme.help: The theme Bugaboo shows when your device is dark. It counts when you choose Match my device.
setting.appearance.spacing.help: How close together things are. Compact fits more on a page.
setting.appearance.larger-text.help: Makes all text a step bigger.
setting.appearance.less-motion.help: Fewer moving effects. Bugaboo also follows the setting of your device.
setting.appearance.issue-view.name: Open issues in
setting.appearance.issue-view.help: Where an issue opens: in the focus view, which gives it most of the page, or in a side panel next to the list.
setting.region.time-zone.name: Time zone
setting.region.time-zone.help: The time zone for the times you see. Match my device uses the time zone of your device.
setting.region.date-format.name: Date format
setting.region.number-format.name: Number format
setting.region.number-format.help: How big numbers and decimals are written.
setting.region.first-day.name: First day of the week
setting.region.first-day.help: The day a week starts on in calendars.
setting.start.page.name: Start page
setting.start.page.help: The page Bugaboo opens after you sign in.
setting.shortcuts.keys.name: Your own keys
setting.shortcuts.keys.help: The keys you chose for keyboard shortcuts. A shortcut you did not change keeps its usual keys.
setting.security.two-step-required.name: Two-step sign-in for everybody
setting.auth.sign-up-enabled.name: Sign up without an invitation
setting.auth.sign-up-domains.name: E-mail domains that may sign up
setting.auth.access-key-default-days.nam: Access key lasts (days), when no date is picked
setting.auth.access-key-longest-days.nam: Longest an access key can last (days)
cookie.session.purpose: Keeps you signed in on this device. Bugaboo removes it when you sign out or when your sign-in runs out.
cookie.csrf.purpose: Protects you from other websites that try to make Bugaboo do something in your name.
server.listening: Bugaboo is running at {address}. Stop it with Ctrl+C.
server.database-built-in: Database: built-in SQLite in the data folder.
server.database-failed: Bugaboo could not open its database: {reason}
server.setup-code: Setup is open. Open Bugaboo in your browser and enter this setup code to make the first administrator: {code}
server.setup-code-hint: The code works once and changes every time Bugaboo starts.
server.self-signed: HTTPS uses a certificate made by Bugaboo, so browsers warn until you trust it. The certificate is in {path}.
server.signal-failed: Bugaboo could not listen for the stop signal (Ctrl+C), so it cannot be stopped cleanly.
server.port-busy: Port {port} is busy or not allowed. Choose another port.
config.file-unreadable: The settings file {path} could not be read: {reason}
config.file-invalid: The settings file {path} is not valid: {reason}
config.file-unknown-key: The settings file {path} has a setting Bugaboo does not know: {name}. Known settings are: {known}.
config.file-wrong-type: The setting {name} in {path} must be a text, a number or a list of texts.
config.port-missing: No port is set. Set port in bugaboo.toml, set BUGABOO_PORT, or start with --port.
config.port-invalid: The port {value} is not a number from 1 to 65535.
config.address-invalid: The address {value} is not an IP address such as 127.0.0.1 or ::1.
config.data-dir-empty: The data folder is empty text. Give the path of a folder.
config.database-invalid: The database address must start with sqlite: or postgres:// (or postgresql://).
config.tls-mode-invalid: The HTTPS mode {value} is not known. Use self-signed, files or off.
config.tls-files-missing: HTTPS mode files needs both tls_cert and tls_key.
config.tls-files-unused: tls_cert and tls_key are only used with HTTPS mode files. Remove them or change the mode.
config.tls-off-public: HTTPS cannot be switched off on {address}, because anyone on the network could read what is sent. Use 127.0.0.1 or ::1, or list the proxy that adds HTTPS in trusted_proxies.
config.public-url-invalid: The public address {value} is not a web address like https://bugaboo.example.com.
config.public-url-needed: Bugaboo listens on {address}, so it cannot know the address people type in the browser. Set public_url, for example https://bugaboo.example.com.
config.public-url-proxy: A proxy is listed in trusted_proxies, so people reach Bugaboo through the address of the proxy, which Bugaboo cannot know. Set public_url, for example https://bugaboo.example.com.
config.proxy-invalid: The trusted proxy {value} is not an IP address.
config.log-level-invalid: The log level {value} is not known. Use error, warn, info or debug.
data-folder.create-failed: The data folder {path} could not be prepared: {reason}
data-folder.protect-failed: The data folder {path} could not be made private to its owner: {reason}
data-folder.account-unknown: the account that runs Bugaboo could not be identified
tls.read-failed: The file {path} could not be read: {reason}
tls.write-failed: The file {path} could not be written: {reason}
tls.no-certificate: The file {path} has no certificate in it.
tls.no-key: The file {path} has no private key in it.
tls.unusable: The certificate and the private key cannot be used: {reason}
tls.generate-failed: Bugaboo could not make a certificate: {reason}
config.number-invalid: The setting {name} must be a whole number of 1 or more, not {value}.
tls.key-readable: The private key {path} can be read by other people on this computer. Make it readable by the account that runs Bugaboo only.
server.web-app-missing: The browser app is not built yet. Run `cargo xtask build`, or pass --web <folder>.
server.keys-missing: The data folder has stored secrets or a security log, but its key files in the keys folder are missing. Restore them from your backup. Bugaboo does not make new keys, because the stored secrets could never be read again.
server.about: Bugaboo: the issue tracker in one file
cli.about.openapi: Print the description of the API (OpenAPI) and stop
cli.about.setup: Answer a few questions and save the answers in the settings file
cli.about.service: Run Bugaboo as a service that starts with the computer
cli.about.service-install: Install the service and start it
cli.about.service-uninstall: Stop the service and remove it. Your data stays where it is
cli.about.security-log-verify: Check that nobody changed the security log
cli.about.rotate-key: Make a new master key and use it for every stored secret
cli.about.keys-export: Copy the key files into a folder, for your backup
cli.help.config: The settings file (default: bugaboo.toml next to the program, if it exists)
cli.help.address: The address to listen on (default 127.0.0.1, this computer only)
cli.help.data-dir: The folder that holds all data
cli.help.database-url: The database: sqlite:<file> or postgres://<address> (default: the one inside the data folder)
cli.help.tls: HTTPS mode: self-signed, files or off
cli.help.tls-cert: The certificate file, for HTTPS mode files
cli.help.tls-key: The private key file, for HTTPS mode files
cli.help.public-url: The web address people type to reach Bugaboo, like https://bugaboo.example.com
cli.help.web: Serve the browser app from this folder instead of the one built into the program
cli.help.non-interactive: Ask nothing: use the options given here and the defaults
cli.help.overwrite: Replace the settings file if it already exists
cli.help.keys-folder: The folder to copy the key files into. It is made if it does not exist
cli.no-data: There is no Bugaboo data in {path}. Check the data folder in your settings.
setup.welcome: Welcome to Bugaboo. A few questions, then your answers are saved in a settings file. Press Enter to accept the answer in brackets.
setup.ask.data-dir: Where should Bugaboo keep its data? Give the path of a folder.
setup.ask.address: Who should be able to open Bugaboo? Type 127.0.0.1 for this computer only, or 0.0.0.0 for everyone who can reach this computer.
setup.ask.port: Which port should Bugaboo listen on?
setup.ask.tls: How should the connection be secured (HTTPS)? Type self-signed to let Bugaboo make its own certificate, files to use a certificate you already have, or off for plain HTTP (only on this computer or behind a proxy).
setup.ask.tls-key: Where is the private key file?
setup.ask.public-url: Which web address will people type to reach Bugaboo? For example https://bugaboo.example.com
setup.ask.database: Which database? Type built-in for the database inside the data folder, or a sqlite: or postgres:// address.
setup.ask.replace: The settings file {path} already exists. Replace it? Type yes or no.
setup.exists: The settings file {path} already exists. Add --overwrite to replace it.
setup.input-ended: The questions were not all answered, so nothing was saved.
setup.next: Start Bugaboo with: bugaboo serve. The first start shows a setup code in that window. You need it to make the first administrator in your browser.
setup.service-hint: To have Bugaboo start with the computer, run: bugaboo service install
security-log.valid: The security log is intact: {entries, plural, one {# entry} other {# entries}} checked.
security-log.head: The last entry is number {seq}. Its hash starts with {hash}. Keep a copy of this to compare later.
security-log.unanchored: Nothing vouches for the end of the log, because its anchor file is missing or empty. Someone could cut entries off the end without anybody noticing.
security-log.broken: The security log is broken at entry {seq}: {reason}
security-log.unreadable: The security log could not be read.
security-log.reason.gap: an entry is missing, appears twice or is out of order.
security-log.reason.broken-link: an entry does not match the entry before it.
security-log.reason.changed-content: an entry was changed after it was written.
security-log.reason.checkpoint: entries were deleted without a signed checkpoint, or the checkpoint is wrong.
security-log.reason.truncated: entries at the end of the log were cut off or rewritten.
security-log.reason.anchor: the anchor file that vouches for the end of the log was changed.
security-log.reason.behind: the database lacks the newest entries that the anchor file knows of. Check whether the database was restored from an older backup or lost its last writes. If neither happened, somebody removed entries.
keys.rotated: Made a new master key and used it for {secrets, plural, one {# stored secret} other {# stored secrets}}. Back up the key files again.
keys.exported: Copied the key files into {path}. They can read everything Bugaboo stores in secret: keep them in a safe place, away from the database backup.
keys.export-exists: The folder {path} already holds a copy of a key file. Choose another folder, so no copy is overwritten.
keys.export-failed: The key files could not be copied: {reason}
service.needs-admin: Installing or removing a service needs administrator rights. On Windows, open the terminal as an administrator. On Linux, run the command with sudo.
service.unsupported: Bugaboo can run as a service on Windows and on Linux with systemd. This computer has neither.
service.no-settings: There is no settings file at {path}. Run bugaboo setup first, or name the file with --config.
service.installed: The service {name} is installed and started. It runs as the account {account} and starts with the computer.
service.setup-code: Nobody has made an administrator yet. The setup code for the first administrator is saved in {path}. Read it there, and enter it in your browser.
service.exists: The service {name} is installed already. Remove it first with: bugaboo service uninstall
service.removed: The service {name} is removed. Your data stays where it is.
service.not-a-service: This command is for the service manager. To start Bugaboo yourself, use: bugaboo serve
server.setup-code-file: Setup is open. The setup code is saved in {path}. Read it there and enter it in your browser to make the first administrator.
service.stop-timeout: The service {name} did not stop in time. Stop it in the Services window and try again.
validation.email: Type an e-mail address like name@example.com.
field.password-help: At least 12 characters. A few words in a row make a good password.
field.name: Your name
field.confirm-password-help: Type your password again to make sure it is you.
home.title: Welcome, {name}
home.intro: You are signed in. Projects and issues come with the next versions of Bugaboo. For now you can look after your account.
home.admin: You can look after this server. Organization settings shows what you may do there.
page.not-found.title: This page does not exist
page.not-found.text: The address may be mistyped, or the page may have moved.
sign-in.title: Sign in to Bugaboo
second-step.title: One more step
second-step.intro: Your password is right. Your account asks for a second check before it opens.
second-step.code-help: Type the six-digit code from your code app. If you cannot use the app, type one of your backup codes.
second-step.passkey-help: Use the fingerprint, face or screen lock of this device.
sign-up.title: Make an account
sign-up.closed: Making your own account is switched off here. Ask an administrator to invite you.
invitation.title: Join Bugaboo
invitation.intro: You are invited. Your account will use the e-mail address {email}.
invitation.incomplete: This link is not complete. Open the whole link that you were sent.
first-run.title: Welcome to Bugaboo
first-run.code.intro: Bugaboo was just installed, so nobody has an account yet. To make sure that only you can make the first one, Bugaboo shows a setup code where it is running.
first-run.code.where: Look in the window where Bugaboo is running for the line that starts with Setup is open. If Bugaboo runs as a service, the code is in the file setup-code.txt inside its data folder.
first-run.code.label: Setup code
first-run.code.help: It looks like k7q2-x9mf-3hd8-vt4w. Capital letters and hyphens do not matter.
first-run.account.title: Make the first administrator
first-run.account.intro: An administrator can invite people and look after the server. This account is the first one.
first-run.safer.title: Keep your account safe
first-run.safer.intro: A password alone can be guessed or stolen. You can add a second check now, or later in Sign-in & security.
first-run.done.title: You are all set
first-run.done.text: Your account is ready and you are signed in.
security.title: Sign-in & security
security.intro: How you prove that it is you, and how to keep your account safe.
security.password.title: Password
security.password.changed: Your password is changed. You are signed out everywhere else.
passkeys.title: Passkeys
passkeys.intro: A passkey lets you sign in with the fingerprint, face or screen lock of your device instead of typing a password. It can also be your second step.
passkeys.unavailable: Passkeys need Bugaboo to be opened with a web address that has a name, not a number. Ask the person who runs Bugaboo to set the public address.
passkeys.name: Name for this passkey
passkeys.remove-text: You can no longer sign in with this passkey. Type your password to confirm.
passkeys.cancelled: The passkey was not used. You can try again.
code-app.title: Code app
code-app.intro: A code app on your phone shows a new six-digit code every 30 seconds. You type it after your password.
code-app.on: The code app is set up.
code-app.off: The code app is not set up.
code-app.scan: Scan this picture with your code app.
code-app.qr-alt: QR picture for your code app
code-app.key-label: Cannot scan? Type this key into your app
code-app.confirm-help: Type the six-digit code that the app shows now.
code-app.switched-on: The code app is switched on. Save your backup codes now.
code-app.turn-off-text: Your account will be less safe. Type your password to confirm.
code-app.turned-off: The code app is switched off.
backup.title: Backup codes
backup.intro: Each backup code works once. They are for when you cannot use your code app. Keep them somewhere safe.
backup.left: {count, plural, one {# backup code is left} other {# backup codes are left}}.
backup.shown-once: These codes are shown only now. Save them before you leave this page.
sessions.title: Where you're signed in
sessions.intro: Each line is a place where you are signed in, like a browser. Sign out of the ones you do not know.
sessions.list: Places where you are signed in
sessions.unknown-device: A browser we do not know
sessions.everywhere-text: You will be signed out of every browser, this one included, and have to sign in again. Your access keys are deleted and stop working too.
sessions.cut-off: Only the newest places are shown.
invitations.title: Invitations
invitations.intro: An invitation is a link that lets one person make their account. It works once and runs out after 7 days.
invitations.link-help: Bugaboo cannot send e-mail yet. Copy this link and send it to the person. It is shown only now.
sign-up-policy.title: Signing up without an invitation
sign-up-policy.intro: When this is on, anyone who can open Bugaboo can make an account without being invited.
sign-up-policy.switch: Let people make their own account
sign-up-policy.domains: E-mail domains that may sign up
sign-up-policy.domains-help: One domain per line, like example.com. Only addresses of these domains can sign up.
sign-up-policy.warning: No domain is listed, so everyone who can reach Bugaboo can make an account. Bugaboo cannot check that an address belongs to the person until it can send e-mail.
sign-up-policy.confirm-text: No domain is listed. Everybody who can reach Bugaboo will be able to make an account.
server-status.title: Server status
server-status.intro: How this Bugaboo server is doing.
server-status.uptime: {days, plural, one {# day} other {# days}}, {hours, plural, one {# hour} other {# hours}}, {minutes, plural, one {# minute} other {# minutes}}
server-status.database.built-in: The built-in database in the data folder
server-status.certificate.valid: Valid until {date}, which is {days, plural, one {# day} other {# days}} from now.
server-status.certificate.soon: Valid until {date}, which is only {days, plural, one {# day} other {# days}} from now. Renew it soon.
server-status.certificate.expired: This certificate ran out on {date}. Browsers refuse it.
server-status.certificate.none: Not shown. Either another program in front of Bugaboo handles HTTPS, or the certificate file cannot be read.
server.setup-code-file-failed: Setup is open, but the setup code could not be saved in {path}: {reason}. Stop Bugaboo and start it in a terminal with: bugaboo serve. The terminal shows the code.
keys.not-owner: The data folder {path} belongs to the account {owner}, and you are using another one. A command run from here could leave files that the Bugaboo service cannot read. Run it as {owner}: {how}
keys.no-access: This account cannot read and change the key files in {path}. If Bugaboo runs as a service, run the command as the account that runs it: {how}
keys.how-windows: On Windows that account is {owner}. It has no password, so you cannot sign in as it: stop the service, start a terminal as that account with a tool that can do this, and run: {command}
keys.export-not-private: The folder {path} can be opened by other accounts on this computer. Choose a folder that only you can open, or a new one, so the key files are not left where others can copy them.
data-folder.not-a-data-folder: The folder {path} has other files in it and does not look like a Bugaboo data folder. Installing the service would change who owns them. Choose an empty folder or a Bugaboo data folder as the data folder in your settings.
service.settings-is-link: The settings file {path} is a link. Installing would change the rights of the file it points to. Name the real file with --config.
service.settings-in-data: The settings file {path} is inside the data folder, which the account that runs the service can write to. Move the file out of the data folder, so that the service cannot change its own settings.
service.settings-folder-open: The folder {path} that holds the settings file can be changed by other accounts. Keep the settings file in a folder that only administrators can change, for example /etc/bugaboo.
service.settings-folder-owner: The folder {path} that holds the settings file does not belong to the administrator account (root). Keep the settings file in a folder that root owns, for example /etc/bugaboo.
service.data-folder-real: The data folder {path} is a link. The service uses the folder it leads to: {real}.
search.title: Quick search
search.label: Search
search.partial: Some results could not be loaded.
shortcut.list-next: Open the next item in the list
shortcut.list-previous: Open the previous item in the list
shortcut.title: Keyboard shortcuts
shortcut.intro: Press these keys instead of clicking. Every shortcut also has a button on the page.
appearance.title: Appearance
appearance.device-help: Match my device uses one theme when your device is light and one when it is dark. Choose both here.
appearance.light: Theme when my device is light
appearance.dark: Theme when my device is dark
appearance.device-settings: Your device may already ask for less motion or more contrast. Bugaboo follows both. Your choices are kept with you, so they follow you to every browser you sign in from.
shortcuts.intro: Choose the keys you like. Open a shortcut to change its keys.
shortcuts.new-keys-help: Click the box and press the keys you want. For two keys in a row, press one and then the other.
shortcuts.conflict: {keys} is already used for: {action}. Choose other keys.
shortcuts.reserved: Your browser uses these keys for copying, pasting and undoing. Choose other keys.
shortcuts.invalid: These keys cannot be used. Press one key, or two in a row.
markdown.preview-empty: There is nothing to preview yet.
markdown.preview-failed: The preview could not be loaded. Check your connection and try again.
server-status.log-failures: {count, plural, one {# entry} other {# entries}} of the security log could not be written since the server started. Check that the disk is not full and that the account that runs Bugaboo can write in the data folder, then look at the server log.
cli.database-url-password: The database address on the command line has a password in it, and other people on this computer can read the command line, for example in the list of running programs. Put database_url in your settings file ({file}) or in the environment variable {variable} instead, and leave the option out.
data-folder.open: {part} {path} can be opened by other accounts on this computer. Bugaboo leaves it as it is, in case you set these rights on purpose. If nobody else should read it, remove the rights of the other accounts: on Linux run chmod go-rwx on it, on Windows open the Security tab of its properties.
server-status.data-folder.closed: Only the account that runs Bugaboo can open the parts of the data folder.
server-status.data-folder.open: Other accounts on this computer can open these. Bugaboo leaves them as they are, in case you set these rights on purpose. If nobody else should read them, remove the rights of the other accounts.
data-folder.own-certificate: The folder {path} holds only files of your own in its tls folder, such as a certificate. Installing the service would change who owns them. If this folder is meant to become the data folder of Bugaboo, run the command again with {flag}.
cli.help.take-over-data-folder: Take over a data folder that holds only your own files in its tls folder, such as a certificate you put there before the first start
setup.database-url-password: The database address on the command line has a password in it, and other people on this computer can read the command line, for example in the list of running programs. This time the address is saved in {file}. Next time answer the database question of setup instead of using the option, or set the environment variable {variable}.
data-folder.unknown: {part} {path} could not be checked, because Bugaboo could not read its access rights. Check them yourself: other accounts on this computer should not be able to open it, unless you want that.
server-status.data-folder.unknown: Bugaboo could not read the rights of these, so it cannot say whether other accounts can open them. Check them yourself:
error.access.would-lock-out: That would leave nobody who can manage roles and decide who has which role for the whole organization. Keep at least one person who can do both.
error.access.cannot-lift: This group has No access in a project that you cannot decide in. Taking people out of it, or deleting it, would lift that No access, so ask somebody who decides there.
error.access.too-much: You can only add or give what you can do yourself in this place.
error.setting.hosts-not-bare: Write only the host names, like images.example.com, without https:// and without a path.
error.setting.locked: An administrator locked this setting, so it can't be changed here.
error.assignment.conflict: This person or group already has a role here, so it cannot also have No access here, and the other way round. Take the other row away first.
error.name.taken: That name is already used. Choose another one.
error.project.move-lifts-no-access: This move would let somebody take away a No access that applies to them. Take that No access away first, or move the project somewhere else.
error.project.too-deep: Projects cannot be nested any deeper than this. Make or move it somewhere higher up.
error.project.move-into-itself: A project cannot go inside itself or inside one of its own sub-projects.
error.project.preview-changed: The projects, or who has which role, changed since you looked at the preview. Look at it again before you move the project.
access-keys.title: Access keys
access-keys.intro: An access key lets a script or an app work as you. It can do at most what you can do, and it always runs out. You see a key once, when you make it.
access-keys.empty: You have no access keys yet.
access-keys.name: Name
access-keys.name-help: What the key is for, like “Nightly report”.
access-keys.help.see-only: The key can look at what you can look at, and it can change nothing.
access-keys.help.see-and-change: The key can also change what you may change, but it cannot manage people, roles or settings.
access-keys.help.everything: The key can do all that you can do, except what no key can do.
access-keys.never: No key can invite people, change who has which role, change the settings of the organization, or change how you sign in. You do that here, where you are signed in.
access-keys.help.permissions: The key can do only what you tick below, and only what you can do yourself.
access-keys.projects-help: Tick none for every project. A key for some projects works in them and in the projects inside them, and gives nothing for the whole organization.
access-keys.projects-none: You have no projects to choose from yet.
access-keys.expires-help: Without another day, the key runs out in {days, plural, one {# day} other {# days}}. The latest day is {latest}.
access-keys.shown-once: Copy the key now and keep it safe. Bugaboo shows it only this once and cannot show it again.
access-keys.row.permissions: {count, plural, one {# single permission} other {# single permissions}}
access-keys.delete-text: Anything that uses it stops working at once. A deleted key cannot come back.
set-up-second-step.title: Set up your second step
set-up-second-step.why: Your administrator asks you to sign in with a second step. It keeps your account safe even if somebody learns your password.
set-up-second-step.how: Choose a code app or a passkey below. When one of them is set up, you can go on.
set-up-second-step.ready: Your second step is set up.
access-keys.pick-one: Tick at least one permission, or switch single permissions off.
permission.see-projects: See the project and what is in it
permission.see-issues: See every issue of the project, not only the ones they reported
permission.change-issues: Change anybody's issues, in the fields they may change
permission.change-own-issues: Change the issues they reported, in the fields they may change
permission.comment: Write comments on the issues they see
permission.move-issues: Move issues into or out of the project
permission.edit-anyway: Take over text somebody else is editing; their text is kept
permission.manage-issue-types: Manage issue types, kinds of relation and layouts
permission.manage-labels: Manage labels and tags, also rename and combine them
permission.make-projects: Make projects at the top level
permission.move-projects: Move sub-projects into or out of the project
permission.change-project-settings: Change the project's name, short name and settings
permission.decide-roles: Decide who has which role, including No access
permission.decide-what-roles-see: Decide which fields and which people information each role sees
permission.check-access: Check what other people can do, and why
permission.manage-people: See everybody's e-mail address and correct their names
permission.manage-invitations: Invite people and take invitations back
permission.manage-groups: Make, rename and delete groups and change who is in them
permission.see-status: See how the server is doing
issue-field.title: Title
projects.heading: Projects
projects.tree-empty: You do not see any project yet.
projects.title: Projects
projects.intro: The projects you can see. Open one to change its name or short name. A project is moved on its own settings page.
projects.nothing: No project found. Try another word.
projects.none-yet: There is no project yet. Make the first one below.
projects.make-intro: A project at the top level. Sub-projects are made inside their project.
projects.field-short-name-help: 2 to 10 letters or digits, starting with a letter. It starts the issue IDs and is the address, like WEB.
projects.short-name-change-help: The old short name stays with this project: its old addresses keep working, and nobody else can take it.
projects.short-name-fixed: You can change the name here. Changing the short name takes the right to make projects where this project sits.
projects.sub-projects-empty: This project has no sub-projects yet.
projects.sub-projects-ask: Ask a project lead if you need one.
projects.move-text: Put {name}, with everything inside it, into another project, or at the top level. You read what changes before it happens.
projects.move-dialog-text: Pick where it goes, then read what changes for people before you confirm.
projects.picker-nothing: No project found. Try another word.
projects.preview-nothing: Nobody gains or loses access, and nobody changes role.
projects.preview-hidden-note: This list holds only the projects you can see. People may be affected in projects you cannot see.
projects.preview-truncated: There are more changes than this list shows.
projects.preview-blocked-out-of-sight: Something in a project you cannot see also stands in the way. Ask somebody who sees more to look at this move.
projects.line-held-back-ends: In {project}, a No access no longer holds {person} back.
projects.line-held-back-starts: In {project}, a No access now holds {person} back.
projects.line-lift: {person} could take away the No access that applies to them in {project}. Take that No access away first, or move the project somewhere else.
cli.about.sample: Make the sample organization: fictional people, the same every time from a seed
cli.help.sample-seed: The number the sample is made from. The same number makes the same organization
cli.help.sample-start: The moment the sample ends, in seconds since 1 January 1970. The program never reads the clock, so the same moment makes the same dates
cli.help.sample-database: Where the sample is kept: sqlite (a file in the data folder) or postgres (the address of an empty database is in the environment variable {variable})
cli.help.sample-out: The folder for the data folder, the sign-in details and the dump of the sample
sample.done: Made the sample organization with {people} people from seed {seed}. Data folder: {folder}. How to sign in as them: {file}
sample.sign-in-header:
Sample organization: how to sign in.
The passwords are random and belong to this run only. Never copy this file anywhere.
One line per person, separated by tabs: e-mail address, password, role, name, the secret of the code app (empty for people who have none), and the access key for the few people who have one.
sample.error.names: The list of names cannot be used: {reason}
sample.error.random: The system gave no secure random numbers for the passwords.
sample.error.not-a-sample-folder: The folder {path} has other things in it and was not made by this tool, so it is left alone. Choose another folder or empty this one.
sample.error.step: A step of the sample was refused ({step}): {reason}
sample.error.log-broken: The security log of the sample does not verify: entry {seq}, {reason}
sample.error.start: The start moment {start} is not a moment in time.
sample.error.database-url: The environment variable {variable} must hold the address of an empty PostgreSQL database.
sample.step.region: choosing the region of a person
sample.step.group-member: putting a person into a group
sample.error.names-repeated: The list of names is empty, or names a first name or a family name twice.
sample.error.name-not-letters: The name {name} has other characters than the letters a to z, so it cannot be part of an e-mail address.
sample.error.too-few-names: The list of names is too short for {people} different people.
sample.error.setup-closed: Setup was closed already, so the setup code does not work.
sample.error.secret-not-stored: The secret of the code app was not stored.
sample.error.person-missing: A person of the plan has no account in the database.
sample.error.log-not-anchored: Nothing vouches for the end of the security log: its anchor file is missing.
sample.error.layout: The file tools/dev/sample.json is not usable: {reason}
sample.error.link-missing: The answer to an invitation does not say where to open it.
sample.error.key-missing: The answer to a new access key does not hold the key.
sample.error.not-made: {name} is not in the database although it was made just now.
error.role.in-use: Somebody has this role. Choose the role that takes its place before you delete it.
people.intro: Everybody who has an account. Open a person to see the groups they are in and the roles they have.
people.list-ask: The list of everybody is for people who manage people. Ask an administrator if you need it.
people.search: Search people by name or e-mail address
person.roles-none: {name} has no role in the places you decide about.
person.roles-where: You see the roles in the whole organization and in the projects where you decide who has which role. Change them in Roles & permissions and in the settings of a project.
groups.intro: A group is a set of people. Give a role to a group, and everybody in it has that role.
groups.none-yet: There are no groups yet. Make the first one below.
groups.nothing: No group found. Try another word.
groups.make-intro: A new group is empty. Put people into it afterwards.
groups.made: The group {name} is made. Open it in the list to put people into it.
groups.gone: This group does not exist any more.
groups.members-none: Nobody is in this group yet.
groups.add-list: People you can put into the group
groups.used-projects: {count, plural, one {in # project you can see} other {in # projects you can see}}
groups.used-nothing: Not used for the whole organization or in a project you can see.
groups.delete-text: This deletes the group and takes away every role and every No access it was given. {members, plural, one {The # person in it stays} other {The # people in it stay}} and keep the roles they have in other ways. This cannot be taken back.
roles.intro: A role is a set of permissions, given to people or groups. Open a role to change what it allows.
roles.make-intro: Start from an empty role, or from a copy of the role that is closest to what you need. Then choose what it allows.
roles.permissions-intro: Tick what people with this role may do. A change is saved at once.
roles.counts-organization: Counts only when the role is given for the whole organization.
roles.two-step: Two-step sign-in for everyone with this role
roles.two-step-help: People with this role must set up a code app or a passkey before they can do anything else.
roles.second-step-gap: {count, plural, one {# person with this role has not set up a second step yet.} other {# people with this role have not set up a second step yet.}}
roles.reset-help: This is a starting role. You can give it back the permissions it had at the start.
roles.reset-text: The permissions and the two-step switch of {name} go back to what they were at the start. The name stays. What was changed since is lost.
roles.copy-help: Make a new role that starts with the permissions of this one.
roles.delete-unused: Nobody has this role. It is deleted at once and cannot come back.
roles.delete-used: Choose the role that takes its place: everybody who has this role gets the other one, in the same place and with the same reach. This cannot be taken back.
roles.replace-help: Rows that give this role give the role you choose instead.
roles.used: Used {places}: {people, plural, =0 {no people} one {# person} other {# people}} and {groups, plural, =0 {no groups} one {# group} other {# groups}} have it.
roles.used-by-nobody: Used {places}. Nobody has it by name or through a group.
roles.used-projects: {count, plural, one {in # project you can see} other {in # projects you can see}}
roles.used-nothing: Nobody has this role in a place you can see.
roles.from-hidden: from a project you can't see
assignments.title-organization: Who has which role in the whole organization
assignments.intro-organization: The people and groups with a role in the whole organization. A role given here counts in every project.
assignments.intro-project: The people and groups with a role here. A row that comes from a parent project says so; change it for this project by giving a row here. No access hides this project and its sub-projects, whatever role comes from above.
assignments.none: Nobody has a role here yet.
assignments.no-access-help: No access covers this project and its sub-projects. It wins over any role from above and over a role through a group on this project. A role given on a sub-project still counts there.
assignments.incomplete: Choose whom to give it to, and which role.
own.ask-title: This takes away your own way to manage roles
own.ask-text: {lost} The organization always keeps somebody who can manage roles, but it may no longer be you.
own.lost-manage-roles: You could no longer make, change or delete roles.
own.lost-decide-roles: You could no longer decide who has which role.
access.origin-unset: Nothing set, so it is hidden
access.ceiling: You can set a level only up to your own. Levels above it cannot be picked.
access.roles-cut: There are more roles than fit in this table. The first ones are shown.
access.role-chooser: Show the levels of the role
field-permissions.intro: For each role, choose whether a field is hidden, can be seen or can be changed. Hidden means the field does not exist for that role: not in issues, searches, e-mails, maps or the assistant.
field-permissions.intro-project: These levels count in {project} and in its sub-projects, until one of them sets its own. Change a level that comes from higher up to set one for this project, and reset it to take that back.
field-permissions.table-name: Which level each role has for each field
people-visibility.intro: For each role and each kind of people information, choose whether people are shown by name, by their role only (a Team member) or not at all (Someone).
people-visibility.intro-project: These levels count in {project} and in its sub-projects, until one of them sets its own. Change a level that comes from higher up to set one for this project, and reset it to take that back.
people-visibility.table-name: How each role sees each kind of people information
check-access.intro: Choose a person and where to look. You read what they can do there, every field and how they see people, each with the reason.
check-access.person-nothing: No person found. People whose names you cannot see are not listed.
check-access.place-nothing: No project found. Try another word.
check-access.pick-a-person: Pick a person to read what they can do.
check-access.reason.role-person-organiza: {person} has the role {role} for the whole organization.
check-access.reason.role-group-organizat: {person} is in the group {group}, which has the role {role} for the whole organization.
check-access.reason.role-group-project: {person} is in the group {group}, which has the role {role} in {project}.
check-access.reason.inherited-project: {place} is inside {project}, so the role applies here too.
check-access.reason.inherited-organizati: The role is given for the whole organization, so it applies here too.
check-access.reason.blocked-person: But {person} has No access in {project}, and that wins over the role.
check-access.reason.blocked-group: But {person} is in the group {group}, which has No access in {project}, and that wins over the role.
check-access.reason.kept: Deciding who has which role stays, because it comes from higher up. Nobody is locked out of managing roles.
check-access.reason.organization-only: The role {role} has this, but it counts only when the role is given for the whole organization.
check-access.reason.narrowed-by-key: The access key does not keep this.
check-access.reason.outside-key: The access key does not count in this project.
check-access.reason.none: No role {person} has here gives this.
check-access.level.no-role: {person} has no role here, so nothing is shown.
check-access.level.capped: The access key lowers it to Can see.
check-access.level.role-organization: The role {role} gives {level} for the whole organization.
check-access.level.role-unset: The role {role} sets nothing, so it counts as hidden.
check-access.all-other-kinds: All other kinds of people information
check-access.group-the-same: Group those with the same reason
relation-kinds.intro: A kind of relation says what a connection between two issues means, in words for both ends: blocks and is blocked by. Retire a kind to stop new relations of it; the relations that have it keep it.
relation-kinds.nothing: No kind of relation has that name.
relation-kinds.make-intro: Write what the first issue reads and what the second one reads, like blocks and is blocked by. Use the same words twice for a kind that reads alike from both ends.
relation-kinds.made: The kind of relation {name} is made.
relation-kinds.retire-help: A retired kind is not offered for new relations. The relations that have it keep it. You can offer it again later.
relation-kinds.offer-again: Offer the kind of relation again
sub-issues.title: Sub-issues
related-issues.title: Related issues
related-issues.nothing-to-pick: There is no kind of relation to pick. Someone who manages kinds of relation can make one.
history.title: History
history.relation-removed: {who} took away a relation: this issue {name} {issue}
comments.write-help: Type @ and a name to mention someone.
comments.lock-held: Someone else is editing this comment.
mentions.title: Mentions
error.issue.parent-circle: That would make a circle of issues or a chain that is too long. Choose another issue.
error.limit.reached: That is as many as one issue can hold. Take some away first.
error.relation.exists: Those two issues are related in that way already.
error.issue.type-retired: That issue type is retired, so no new issues can be made with it. Choose another type.
setting.issues.id-mode.name: Issue IDs
setting.issues.id-mode.help: Random IDs (like WEB-K7Q2X) hide how many issues there are and how fast they come. Counting IDs (like WEB-142) are easy to say aloud. When you change this, every issue of the project gets a new ID; the old IDs keep working.
setting.issues.id-length.name: Length of random issue IDs
setting.issues.id-length.help: How many letters and digits a random issue ID has after the dash. Between 4 and 8. It grows by itself when the short ones run out.
issue-types.intro: An issue type says what kind of issue it is: a bug, a task, a feature or a goal. Everybody who makes an issue picks one of these. Retire a type to stop new issues of it; the issues that have it keep it.
issue-types.nothing: No issue type has that name.
issue-types.make-intro: A new type goes to the end of the list. Pick an icon so people find it quickly.
issue-types.retire-help: A retired type is not offered for new issues. The issues that have it keep it and can still be changed. You can offer it again later.
error.field.required: This field has to be filled in.
error.field.too-short: That is shorter than this field allows.
error.field.too-long: That is longer than this field allows.
error.field.too-small: That is lower than this field allows.
error.field.too-big: That is higher than this field allows.
error.field.no-match: That does not have the form this field asks for.
error.field.wrong-value: That is not a value this field can hold.
error.field.unknown-choice: That choice is not offered by this field.
error.field.unknown-reference: That person, group or issue cannot be chosen here.
error.field.not-here: This field is not used here.
field-permissions.type-help: These levels count for issues of every type, unless a level is set for one type below.
field-permissions.type-help-chosen: A level set here counts for issues of this type only, and wins over the level for all types. Where nothing is set for this type, the level for all types counts.
fields.intro: Fields are the pieces of information on an issue or a project. Add the fields your organization needs, and decide who sees and fills in each one under Field permissions.
fields.nothing: There are no fields of your own yet. Make one below.
fields.make-intro: Start with what kind of information the field holds. You can change everything else later, except the kind.
fields.field-choices-help: One choice on each line. You can change names, colors and icons on the field page.
fields.field-required: It has to be filled in
fields.never-to-assistant: Never send this field to the assistant
fields.default-help: The value a new issue or project starts with. Leave it empty for none.
fields.choices-help: Use the arrows to change the order. Retire a choice to stop offering it for new values; the values already set stay. Combine a choice with another one to move every value over.
fields.rule-pattern-help: The whole text has to match. For example, [A-Z]+-[0-9]+ matches CAB-12.
fields.rules-not-a-number: One of the rules is not a number in the form this field uses.
fields.look-preview: The look in all four themes
fields.used-everywhere: {count, plural, =0 {No project has a value yet.} one {1 project has a value.} other {# projects have a value.}}
fields.used-in-projects: {count, plural, =0 {Limited to no project you can see.} one {Used in 1 project.} other {Used in # projects.}}
fields.scope-projects-list: Projects the field is limited to
fields.scope-types-help: Tick the issue types that have the field. With none ticked, every issue type has it.
fields.see-help: Each role sees a field as Hidden, Can see or Can change. A new field starts with Can see for everyone who sees the project, and Can change from Team member up.
fields.retire-help: A retired field is no longer offered for new values. The values already set stay on the issues and projects.
fields.not-a-decimal: Type a number, with a point for the decimal part.
fields.not-a-duration: Type a length of time like 1h 30m.
fields.combine-text: Every value of {name} becomes {into}, in every issue and project that has it, and {name} is retired. Each of those issues gets a record in its history. This cannot be taken back.
fields.used-more: {count, plural, one {And # more project.} other {And # more projects.}}
issues.title: Issues
issues.draft-kept: Your draft is kept if you close this window.
issues.draft-found: You have a draft of this description from {when}.
issues.draft-found-form: You have a draft of a new issue from {when}.
issues.nothing: There are no issues here yet.
issues.read-only: Only people whose role allows it can change {field}.
issues.assign-search: Search the people of the project
issues.assign-nothing: Nobody in this project has that name.
issues.assign-only-you: Nobody else is offered here: people you cannot see by name are not listed.
issues.editing-elsewhere: You are editing this description in another window.
issues.changed-after-you: The description changed after you started.
issues.lost-ran-out: Not saved yet: your editing time ran out. Your text is kept.
issues.lost-taken-over: Not saved yet: {name} took over the editing. Your text is kept.
issues.lost-changed: Not saved yet: {name} changed the description after you. Your text is kept.
issues.compare-intro: Your text is next to the newer version. For each paragraph that differs, choose which one to keep.
shortcut.change-status: Change the status of the open issue
shortcut.assign: Choose who the open issue is assigned to
shortcut.edit-description: Edit the description of the open issue
issues.selected: {count, plural, one {# issue is ticked} other {# issues are ticked}}
issues.changed-own: {count, plural, one {# field changed.} other {# fields changed.}}
fields.pick-no-groups: There are no groups you can choose.
fields.pick-issue-key: ID of the issue, like WEB-12
layouts.intro: A layout says which fields a form shows, in which sections, and for which roles. A Guest can get a short form and a Team member the full one. A layout never shows a field to a role whose field permissions hide it.
layouts.not-customized: This form has not been customized yet. It shows the usual fields to every role.
layouts.inherited-organization: This form uses the layout of the whole organization.
layouts.inherited-project: This form uses the layout of {project}.
layouts.use-inherited-text: The layout of this place is taken away. The place then uses the layout it inherits. This cannot be undone.
layouts.fixed: The title and the issue type are always asked for.
layouts.section-tab-help: Sections with the same tab are shown together under that tab. Leave it empty for no tabs.
layouts.section-empty: No fields in this section yet. Drag a field here or use its Add button.
layouts.available: Fields that are not on this form
layouts.available-none: Every field is on this form.
layouts.field-required: Required: it stays on the form for everybody who can fill it in.
layouts.unsaved: You have changes that are not saved.
layouts.lost: You are no longer editing this layout. Your changes are kept here. Ask for the lock again to save them.
layouts.inherited-hidden: This form uses a layout that is set higher up.
